title: Lima Environment Variables Schema
description: JSON Schema documenting Lima environment variables and their configuration

LIMA_INSTANCE.description: Specifies the name of the Lima instance to use

LIMA_SHELL.description: Specifies the shell interpreter to use inside the Lima instance
LIMA_SHELL.default: User's shell configured inside the instance

LIMA_TEMPLATES_PATH.description: Specifies the directories used to resolve template:// URLs

LIMA_WORKDIR.description: Specifies the initial working directory inside the Lima instance

LIMA_SHELLENV_ALLOW.description: Specifies a comma-separated list of environment variable patterns to allow when propagating environment variables to the Lima instance with --preserve-env. When set, only variables matching these patterns will be passed through, completely overriding the default block list behavior. This feature only applies to Lima v2.0.0 or later.
notes: Without --preserve-env: No environment variables are propagated (regardless of this setting)
With --preserve-env and LIMA_SHELLENV_ALLOW unset: All variables are propagated except those in the block list
With --preserve-env and LIMA_SHELLENV_ALLOW set: Only variables matching the allow patterns are propagated (block list is ignored)
Patterns support wildcards using * at the end (e.g., CUSTOM_* matches CUSTOM_VAR, CUSTOM_PATH, etc.)

LIMA_SHELLENV_BLOCK.description: Specifies a comma-separated list of environment variable patterns to block when propagating environment variables to the Lima instance with --preserve-env. Can either replace the default block list or extend it by prefixing with +. This feature only applies to Lima v2.0.0 or later.
LIMA_SHELLENV_BLOCK.default: A predefined list of system and shell-specific variables
notes: Default block list includes: BASH*, SHELL, SHLVL, ZSH*, ZDOTDIR, FPATH, PATH, PWD, OLDPWD, TMPDIR, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, UID, GID, EUID, GROUP, HOSTNAME, DISPLAY, TERM, TERMINFO, XAUTHORITY, XDG_*, SSH_*, DYLD_*, LD_*, _*
Use + prefix to add to the default block list rather than replacing it entirely
Patterns support wildcards using * at the end
This variable only affects the --preserve-env flag behavior

LIMACTL.description: Specifies the path to the limactl binary

LIMA_SSH_OVER_VSOCK.description: Specifies to use vsock for SSH connection instead of port forwarding
LIMA_SSH_OVER_VSOCK.deprecationNote: This variable is deprecated in favor of the YAML field .ssh.overVsock (since v2.0.2)
notes: This variable is effective only if the VM is VZ based and systemd is v256 or later (e.g. Ubuntu 24.10+)

LIMA_SSH_PORT_FORWARDER.description: Specifies to use the SSH port forwarder (slow) instead of gRPC (fast, previously unstable)
notes: Version history: v0.1.0 (true), v1.0.0 (false), v1.0.1 (true), v1.1.0+ (false)

LIMA_USERNET_RESOLVE_IP_ADDRESS_TIMEOUT.description: Specifies the timeout duration for resolving the IP address in usernet

_LIMA_QEMU_UEFI_IN_BIOS.description: Commands QEMU to load x86_64 UEFI images using -bios instead of pflash drives
_LIMA_QEMU_UEFI_IN_BIOS.default: false on Unix-like hosts and true on Windows hosts
notes: It is expected that this variable will be set to false by default in future when QEMU supports pflash UEFI for accelerated guests on Windows

_LIMA_WINDOWS_EXTRA_PATH.description: Additional directories which will be added to PATH by limactl.exe process to search for tools. It is useful when there is a need to prevent collisions between binaries available in active shell and ones used by limactl.exe - injecting them only for the running process w/o altering PATH observed by user shell. Is Windows specific and does nothing for other platforms.
notes: This is an experimental setting and has no guarantees being ever promoted to stable. It may be removed or changed at any stage of project development.
